docs.title: pipeloom
docs.text:
Declarative, engine-agnostic data pipelines in YAML.

pipeloom is in its design phase. Version 0.0.2 only reserves the package name.

  • Architecture
  • Architecture decision records

docs.title: pipeloom architecture
docs.text: Status: Design (pre-0.1). Nothing described here is implemented yet. Decisions are recorded as ADRs in adr/. Diagrams are D2 sources in diagrams/ with committed SVGs.

docs.title: 1. Vision, goals, non-goals, principles
docs.text:
Vision. A small, typed framework. Pipelines are declared in YAML and compiled into an immutable plan. That plan runs the same way on pandas, polars, PySpark or later engines, and runs locally, as one Databricks job, or as an Airflow DAG. Every run produces a single event stream and artifacts you can query.

Goals: declarative YAML with layered validation and editor completion; an engine-agnostic core with one plugin per tool; end-to-end events and styled logs; persisted metadata for each run and each model; a Databricks one-job renderer; a cosmos-style Airflow integration; open-source hygiene.

Non-goals (through 1.0): streaming; a scheduler service or UI; a portable SQL dialect; Jinja templating; running user code at compile time; Airflow 2 support.

Principles. Each answers a lesson (L) from the concept spec. 1. One event stream. Logs, metrics, artifacts and lineage subscribe to it (L1). 2. Dependencies are declared, never traced. Tracing is an opt-in static check that warns (L2). 3. No module-level registries. A Project object owns plugins and config (L3). 4. Docs, the CLI reference, the JSON Schema and the error catalog are all generated from code. Every CLI flag has a test (L4). 5. No session-global mutation. Every engine setting lives in a context manager with guaranteed cleanup. Metrics never depend on global commit tags (L5, L10). 6. Ready-queue scheduling with no level barriers (L6). 7. Execution units never share in-memory state. Ephemeral models are inlined; intermediates are persisted (L7). 8. Maintenance operations (compaction, clustering) run only when declared (L8). 9. Each declared write option is either applied by every strategy or rejected at validation (L9). 10. Platform behavior is injected: clock, identity, catalog, secrets (L11). 11. Incremental logic is a declared key plus a lookback, with a watermark store (L12). 12. Retries, timeouts, data quality, persisted metadata, selectors, schema-change policy, SCD2 and deletes are all first-class (L13). 13. YAML first, with JSON Schema (L14).

docs.title: 2. Glossary
docs.text:
• Project: a directory with pipeloom.yml and model files.
  • Model: a named dataset built from declared inputs by a Python callable or a SQL body.
  • Source: an external dataset declared in YAML.
  • Target: a named runtime environment (engine, catalog, naming, state store).
  • Materialization: table, incremental, view, ephemeral or intermediate.
  • Write strategy: append, overwrite, replace_partitions, merge or scd2.
  • Plan: an immutable compiled graph of resolved models.
  • Execution unit: one schedulable node of the plan. It holds one persisted model plus any ephemeral models inlined into it.
  • Boundary: process (all units in one process) or task (each unit in its own process or orchestrator task).
  • Manifest: the serialized plan (manifest.json).
  • Run: one execution of a plan, identified by run_id.
  • Invocation: one process taking part in a run.
  • Attempt: one try of a unit.
  • Watermark: the high-water value of an incremental key.
  • Expectation: a data-quality rule with warn, drop or fail.
  • Sink: an event subscriber.
  • Renderer: turns a plan into an orchestrator artifact.
  • Executor: runs units.
  • Plugin API version: the version of the protocol contract between the core and plugins.

docs.title: 3. Architecture overview
docs.text:
Source: 01-context.d2.

Layers. Arrows point toward dependencies. The core never imports a plugin, and an import-linter contract enforces this in CI.

CLI / Python API (pipeloom.api.Project)
  ├─ config     YAML loader with line marks, pydantic models, schema export
  ├─ validate   layers L0-L7, error catalog
  ├─ graph      DAG, selectors, topological order, cycle paths
  ├─ plan       Plan, ExecutionUnit, Manifest, plan_hash
  ├─ runtime    Scheduler, Executor(thread|process), ModelRunner, ModelContext
  ├─ engine     protocols, logical types, capabilities, portable helpers (Narwhals)
  ├─ incremental / quality / state
  ├─ events     Event models, EventBus, console/jsonl/file sinks
  ├─ artifacts  manifest.json, run_results.json writers
  ├─ secrets    env provider, interpolation, redaction
  ├─ plugins    entry-point discovery, API-version gate
  └─ testing    contract suites, RecordingSink, FakeClock, MemoryEngine
Plugins: pipeloom-pandas | -polars | -spark | -databricks | -airflow | -openlineage

Source: 02-packages.d2.

Lifecycle. Each stage is a pure function from the previous stage's output. Every stage emits events.

  1. Load: discover YAML files, then parse them while recording file, line and column for every node.
  2. Validate schema: pydantic models (L0-L1).
  3. Resolve graph: bind refs and sources, apply defaults and precedence, apply naming strategies to get physical names, apply selectors (L2-L3).
  4. Validate plan: semantics, plugin capabilities and static code checks (L4-L6).
  5. Compile: fuse ephemeral models into units for the chosen boundary, then freeze. Output is Plan plus manifest.json with a plan_hash (sha256 of the canonical JSON, excluding timestamps).
  6. Execute: the scheduler runs units through an executor. Orchestrated tasks run pipeloom run --manifest ... --select unit:<id> --expect-plan-hash <h>.
  7. Finalize: merge per-invocation results, write run_results.json, commit run state, flush and close sinks.

Source: 03-lifecycle.d2.

docs.title: 4. Configuration
docs.text:
Project file.

# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://<docs-site>/schema/v1/project.json
config_version: 1
name: shop
model_paths: [models]
python_paths: [src]            # added to sys.path at execution only
vars: {country: BR}
defaults:
  models: {materialized: table, retries: 1, timeout: 30m}
targets:
  dev:
    engine: {kind: polars}
    catalog: {kind: filesystem, root: ./warehouse}
    naming: {strategy: per_user}
    state: {kind: sqlite, path: .pipeloom/state.db}
    workers: 4
  prod:
    engine: {kind: spark}
    catalog: {kind: unity, catalog: main}
    naming: {strategy: prefix, schema_prefix: prod_}
    state: {kind: table, table: ops._pipeloom_state}
    artifacts: {root: /Volumes/main/ops/pipeloom}
events:
  sinks:
    - {kind: console}
    - {kind: jsonl, path: target/events.jsonl, failure_budget: 5}

Model files. Any *.yml under model_paths.

sources:
  - {name: raw_orders, format: parquet, location: data/raw/orders/}
models:
  - name: stg_orders
    sql: |
      select order_id, customer_id, amount, updated_at from raw_orders
    inputs: {raw_orders: {source: raw_orders}}
  - name: fct_orders
    python: shop.marts.orders:build          # module:function
    inputs:
      orders: {ref: stg_orders}
      customers: {ref: dim_customers}
    materialized: incremental
    incremental: {input: orders, column: updated_at, lookback: 2d}
    write: {strategy: merge, unique_key: [order_id], on_schema_change: append_new_columns}
    partition_by: [order_date]
    expectations:
      - {name: amount_non_negative, check: {range: {column: amount, min: 0}}, on_violation: drop}
    tags: [finance, daily]

models/<dir>/_defaults.yml can set folder-level defaults.

ADR-0003: Model authoring. - Context: L2 and L14 require declared dependencies and YAML validation. Users still need a real transformation language. - Options: YAML-only (too weak for transformations), YAML plus Python, YAML plus SQL, or YAML plus both. - Choice: YAML declares every model. The body is either a Python callable or a SQL body. The inputs map binds local aliases to ref or source. - A Python callable is called as build(ctx, **inputs). Each alias becomes a keyword argument holding a relation. - SQL refers to aliases as table names. The engine registers them as named relations for that query only. - At compile time pipeloom imports nothing from the project. L6 parses the callable's file with ast to check that the function exists and that its parameters equal ctx plus the input aliases. - Opt-in SQL table-reference checking via the sqlglot extra warns on mismatch. - Consequences: graphs are cheap to build, so Airflow can parse DAG files safely. No Jinja. Reads of undeclared tables through ctx.engine.native are a documented escape hatch outside lineage.

JSON Schema. pipeloom schema export --out schemas/ writes project.json and models.json (draft 2020-12, assumed from pydantic v2; verify) from the pydantic models. - Plugin option models (engine, catalog, sink, state) are composed as discriminated unions on kind, using the plugins that are installed. - The docs site publishes per-version schemas built with all first-party plugins. - The modeline above enables completion in editors that use yaml-language-server.

Precedence. - Runtime settings (highest first): CLI flags; PIPELOOM_* environment variables (for example PIPELOOM_TARGET, PIPELOOM_WORKERS); an optional git-ignored user file ~/.pipeloom/profiles.yml with per-target overrides; the targets.<t> block; then top-level project keys. - Model config: the model entry; the nearest _defaults.yml; then defaults.models. - Targets may change runtime keys only (engine options, catalog, naming, state, workers, artifacts). They may not change model semantics, so plans differ across targets only in physical names and runtime settings. - Interpolation: ${env:NAME}, ${env:NAME:-default} and ${var:name} resolve at compile time and are recorded in the manifest. ${secret:provider/path} resolves only at runtime (section 14).

docs.title: 5. Core protocols
docs.text:
from typing import Any, Protocol, Mapping, Sequence, Iterator, ContextManager
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Column: name: str; dtype: str; nullable: bool = True   # logical type: int64, decimal(18,2), timestamp[UTC]...
Schema = tuple[Column, ...]

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Relation:                      # opaque handle; never inspected by core
    native: Any                      # pandas/polars frame, Spark DataFrame...
    engine: str
    lazy: bool

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class EngineCapabilities:
    formats: frozenset[str]; strategies: frozenset[str]
    sql_models: bool; views: bool; idempotent_writes: bool
    cancel: bool; bytes_metrics: bool; portable: bool   # Narwhals-compatible frames

class Engine(Protocol):
    name: str
    capabilities: EngineCapabilities
    def session(self, ctx: "RuntimeContext") -> ContextManager["EngineSession"]: ...  # cleanup guaranteed (L10)

class EngineSession(Protocol):
    native: Any                                        # escape hatch
    def reader(self, fmt: str) -> "Reader": ...
    def materializer(self, strategy: str) -> "Materializer": ...
    def sql(self, query: str, inputs: Mapping[str, Relation]) -> Relation: ...
    def schema(self, rel: Relation) -> Schema: ...
    def count(self, rel: Relation) -> int: ...
    def filter_since(self, rel: Relation, column: str, lower: Any) -> Relation: ...
    def max_value(self, rel: Relation, column: str) -> Any: ...
    def evaluate(self, rel: Relation, checks: Sequence["ExpectationSpec"]) -> "QualityOutcome": ...
    def cancel(self, unit_id: str) -> None: ...        # cooperative; no-op if not capable

class Reader(Protocol):
    def read(self, spec: "ReadSpec") -> Relation: ...            # source or upstream target
class Writer(Protocol):                                           # format-level primitive
    def write(self, rel: Relation, target: "TargetRef", mode: str, opts: "WriteOptions") -> None: ...

class Materializer(Protocol):                                     # one per strategy
    strategy: str
    def materialize(self, rel: Relation, target: "TargetRef", cfg: "WriteConfig",
                    token: str) -> "WriteResult": ...             # token = idempotency key

class Catalog(Protocol):
    def exists(self, target: "TargetRef") -> bool: ...
    def ensure_namespace(self, ns: "Namespace") -> None: ...      # idempotent, cached per invocation
    def table_schema(self, target: "TargetRef") -> Schema | None: ...
    def apply_grants(self, target: "TargetRef", grants: Sequence["Grant"]) -> None: ...
    def maintain(self, target: "TargetRef", ops: Sequence["MaintenanceOp"]) -> None: ...  # explicit (L8)

class MetricsProvider(Protocol):
    def before_write(self, target: "TargetRef") -> "MetricsToken": ...
    def after_write(self, target: "TargetRef", token: "MetricsToken", result: "WriteResult") -> "WriteMetrics": ...

class StateStore(Protocol):
    def get_watermark(self, key: "StateKey") -> "Watermark | None": ...
    def cas_watermark(self, key: "StateKey", expected: "Watermark | None", new: "Watermark") -> bool: ...
    def record_unit(self, run_id: str, result: "UnitResult") -> None: ...
    def get_run(self, run_id: str) -> "RunRecord | None": ...
    def lock(self, scope: str, run_id: str) -> ContextManager[None]: ...

class EventSink(Protocol):
    name: str
    def handle(self, event: "Event") -> None: ...
    def flush(self) -> None: ...
    def close(self) -> None: ...

class Renderer(Protocol):
    name: str
    def render(self, plan: "Plan", options: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Mapping[str, bytes]: ...  # path -> content

class Executor(Protocol):
    boundary: str                                    # "process" | "task"
    def submit(self, unit: "ExecutionUnit", ctx: "RuntimeContext") -> "UnitHandle": ...
    def cancel(self, handle: "UnitHandle") -> None: ...

class Clock(Protocol):
    def now(self) -> datetime: ...                   # timezone-aware UTC
    def monotonic(self) -> float: ...

class IdentityProvider(Protocol):
    def current(self) -> "Identity": ...             # user, host, orchestrator, orchestrator ids

class SecretProvider(Protocol):
    def resolve(self, path: str) -> str: ...

ADR-0002: Engine abstraction. - Context: the spec (section 4) lists coupling in the return type, reads, schema, temporary views, writes, merge, metrics and catalog SQL. - Options: - (a) A hand-written protocol per plugin: full control, more code per engine. - (b) Narwhals as the core abstraction: it has no write, SQL or catalog API, and only lazy PySpark. - (c) Ibis: heavy, its write support is unverified, and it pushes users into an expression API. - (d) A hybrid. - Choice: (d). - The core contract is the hand-written protocols above. Plugins own IO, writes, merge, catalogs, metrics and cancellation. - The core depends on Narwhals (it has no dependencies of its own) only for pipeloom.engine.portable. That module gives default count, filter_since, max_value, schema and evaluate that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins may reuse, through narwhals.stable.v2. - Model bodies receive native frames by default. frame_api: narwhals on a model passes Narwhals frames, so portable models work on any engine with capabilities.portable. - Consequences: no lowest-common-denominator API for Spark users. Engines can override portable defaults for speed. Narwhals stays a replaceable implementation detail.

docs.title: 6. Plugin system and plugin API version
docs.text:
ADR-0004: Discovery. - Options: entry points (stdlib importlib.metadata, the pytest model), pluggy (1:N hook fan-out), or a dbt-style namespace import. - Choice: entry points. pipeloom picks one implementation per role by kind, which is 1-of-N selection, not hook fan-out, so pluggy adds a dependency without a matching need.

Groups: - pipeloom.engines - pipeloom.catalogs - pipeloom.state_stores - pipeloom.sinks - pipeloom.secret_providers - pipeloom.executors - pipeloom.renderers - pipeloom.naming

Each entry point resolves to a PluginSpec(name, kind, api_version: tuple[int, int], factory, config_model, compatible_engines).

Rules: - Discovery reads metadata only. A plugin is imported only when a config names its kind. - pipeloom plugins list imports nothing. - PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 restricts loading to --plugin module:spec. - Duplicate kind names within a group are error PLU002.

Plugin API version. pipeloom.plugins.API_VERSION = (MAJOR, MINOR), independent of the package version. - MINOR covers additive changes: new optional protocol methods with defaults, new capabilities. - MAJOR covers breaking protocol changes. - The core accepts plugins with the same MAJOR and MINOR ≤ its own. Otherwise it raises PLU001 naming the installed and required versions. - Before 1.0 the API is 0.x and any minor may break. Plugin API 1.0 ships with pipeloom 1.0.

docs.title: 7. Validation layers and error catalog
docs.text:
Each finding is a Diagnostic(code, severity, message, hint, location{file,line,col,json_pointer}, context). Diagnostics serialize to JSON. The catalog lives in code (pipeloom.validate.codes) and generates the docs page. Codes are never reused.

Layer Prefix Examples L0 parse PLY PLY001 YAML syntax; PLY002 duplicate key; PLY003 unknown file encoding L1 schema PLS PLS101 unknown field (with "did you mean"); PLS102 type mismatch; PLS103 unsupported config_version; PLS104 literal value in a secret-like field L2 references PLR PLR201 unknown ref (fuzzy suggestion); PLR202 duplicate model name; PLR203 unknown source; PLR204 unknown target or plugin kind L3 graph PLG PLG301 cycle (prints the path); PLG302 self-reference; PLG303 selector matched nothing; PLG304 unknown selector method L4 plan semantics PLP PLP401 merge or scd2 without unique_key; PLP402 incremental without column; PLP403 aggregate expectation with drop; PLP404 incremental.input not in inputs; PLP405 write option not applied by this strategy (L9); PLP406 ephemeral fan-out above threshold (warning) L5 capability PLC PLC501 strategy unsupported by engine; PLC502 SQL model on an engine without SQL; PLC503 boundary: task with a non-shared state store; PLC504 catalog incompatible with engine; PLC505 non-idempotent append with retries > 0 L6 static code PLK PLK601 callable file or function not found; PLK602 parameters do not match inputs; PLK603 SQL references undeclared table (warning, opt-in) L7 preflight (opt-in, connects) PLF PLF701 engine unreachable; PLF702 source missing; PLF703 target schema drift detected Runtime PLX, PLM, PLQ, PLE, PLU PLX101 model raised; PLX102 timeout; PLX103 plan-hash mismatch; PLX104 cancelled; PLM201 write failed; PLM202 schema change rejected; PLM203 watermark CAS conflict; PLQ301 expectation failed; PLE401 sink disabled; PLU001 plugin API mismatch Renderers PLD, PLA PLD001 task limit exceeded; PLD002 submit above 100 tasks; PLA001 unsupported execution mode

Commands: - pipeloom validate runs L0-L6. - --preflight adds L7. - Exit codes: 0 means OK, 1 means errors, 2 means usage error, 130 means interrupted.

docs.title: 8. Execution and scheduler
docs.text:
ADR-0006: Scheduler. A ready-queue scheduler with no level barrier (L6). - When a unit reaches a terminal state, each child's count of pending parents goes down by one. A child whose count reaches zero is enqueued. - Ready units are ordered by descending count of downstream units, then by name, which is deterministic. - workers caps concurrency. pool tags (a later milestone) cap per-resource concurrency.

Unit state machine.

pending → queued → running → succeeded | failed | timed_out | cancelled
                    running → retrying → running
pending → skipped   (an upstream is failed, timed_out or skipped)
pending → cancelled (run cancelled)

Run state machine: created → compiled → running → succeeded | failed | cancelled. A run with warnings is still succeeded.

Source: 04-state-machines.d2.

Policies: - Retries: retries (default 0) and retry_delay (exponential with jitter, capped). Errors classify as transient (IO, connection, engine-declared) or permanent (user code, validation, quality fail). Only transient errors retry unless retry_on: any. - Retry ownership: with boundary: task, the orchestrator owns retries. pipeloom run --select unit:... then runs with internal retries off and reads the attempt number from orchestrator context. - Timeouts: per-unit timeout. - The thread executor cannot kill threads. On timeout it marks the unit timed_out, calls EngineSession.cancel(unit_id) (for example a Spark job-group or Spark Connect interrupt tag) and discards any late result. - The process executor kills the child process. - Cancellation: SIGINT or SIGTERM stops dequeuing, cancels running units, waits cancel_grace (default 30 s), then marks the rest cancelled. Exit code 130. - Failure isolation: skip-downstream is the default. Independent branches continue. --fail-fast stops dequeuing after the first failure. - Concurrency guard: StateStore.lock("<project>/<target>") blocks a second concurrent run on the same target. --no-lock is the escape hatch.

ADR-0007: Data handoff. - Context: L7. With boundary: task, no in-memory or temporary-view handoff is possible. - Options: persisted intermediates everywhere (simple, costs IO); inlining (free IO, recomputes); a hybrid. - Choice: the hybrid, decided at compile time. - ephemeral models are inlined. Their bodies run inside each consuming unit. Under boundary: process the result is memoized per run, so it is computed once. - intermediate models are persisted to <artifacts.root>/runs/<run_id>/intermediate/<model> (or a scratch schema the catalog provides). Finalize deletes them after intermediate_ttl. - view creates a catalog view where the engine supports it, never a session view. - Consequences: the same plan runs in one process or many. PLP406 warns when an ephemeral model fans out to more than ephemeral_fanout_warn (default 3) units and suggests intermediate.

docs.title: 9. Incremental processing, write strategies, schema change
docs.text:
ADR-0008: Incremental and state. A declared key plus a lookback (L12), with watermarks in a StateStore.

Incremental config:

incremental: {input: orders, column: updated_at, lookback: 2d, watermark_source: state}  # or: target

Algorithm per unit: 1. is_incremental is true when the materialization is incremental, the target exists, the run is not a full refresh, and a watermark exists. 2. Read w = state.get_watermark(project, target, model). With watermark_source: target, read max(column) of the target instead. 3. The input relation becomes filter_since(input, column, w - lookback). The body sees ctx.is_incremental, ctx.watermark and ctx.lower_bound. 4. Write, then cas_watermark(expected=w, new=max_value(filtered input)). A CAS failure is PLM203.

The watermark is committed after the write. A crash between the two reprocesses at most the lookback window plus the batch. That is safe for merge, overwrite and replace_partitions, and for append only when the engine has idempotent writes (otherwise PLC505 forbids retries).

State stores: - sqlite: core, local, single host. - json: core, a directory; atomic rename for local and volume paths. - table: a spark-plugin table in the catalog. boundary: task requires table or json on a shared path.

Write strategies. All return WriteResult(rows_inserted, rows_updated, rows_deleted, rows_written, bytes_written, target_version), with fields None when unknown.

Strategy Semantics Full refresh append insert all rows overwrite overwrite replace data and schema same replace_partitions replace partitions present in the batch (partition_by required) overwrite merge unique_key equality; optional update_condition; deletes: {column, value, mode: hard|soft} overwrite scd2 unique_key, tracked_columns (default all), columns valid_from, valid_to, is_current, row hash; deletes close the current row rebuild

Idempotency: each write receives token = "<run_id>:<model>". Engines with transactional idempotency use it (for Delta, an app id per model and a monotonic version from the run start epoch). Engines without it declare idempotent_writes=False.

Schema-change policy (on_schema_change): - fail (default): any column added, removed or changed in type raises PLM202. - ignore: write the target's columns only. - append_new_columns: add new nullable columns. - sync_all_columns: add and drop columns, and widen types where the engine can.

Every detected change emits schema.changed with a diff.

Table properties, partition_by, clustering and grants are applied by every strategy or rejected (PLP405). Maintenance (optimize, vacuum, clustering changes) runs only from maintenance: blocks with an explicit schedule (every_n_runs), never by default (L8).

docs.title: 10. Data quality
docs.text:
ADR-0009: Expectations. DLT-style actions plus quarantine, evaluated after the transformation and before the write.

expectations:
  - {name: id_not_null, check: {not_null: [order_id]}, on_violation: fail}
  - {name: status_known, check: {accepted_values: {column: status, values: [new, paid, shipped]}}, on_violation: drop}
  - {name: amount_ok, expr: "amount >= 0 and amount < 1e6", on_violation: warn}   # engine-dialect, non-portable
  - {name: unique_id, check: {unique: [order_id]}, on_violation: fail}            # aggregate
quality: {quarantine: true, max_drop_ratio: 0.05}
  • Row-level checks: not_null, accepted_values, range, regex, expr. Allowed actions: warn, drop, fail.
  • Aggregate checks: unique, row_count {min,max}, freshness {column, max_age}. Allowed actions: warn, fail; drop is PLP403.
  • Evaluation: EngineSession.evaluate computes every row-level predicate in one aggregate pass and returns per-expectation passed and failed counts. Unlike DLT, counts are kept on fail too.
  • Drop: filters rows that fail any drop predicate. If max_drop_ratio is exceeded, the unit fails with PLQ301.
  • Quarantine: dropped rows go to <target>__quarantine with _pipeloom_run_id, _pipeloom_failed (array of expectation names) and _pipeloom_ts.
  • Lazy engines may cache the relation before the counting pass. The engine decides; Spark can persist it, and the decision is recorded in the metadata.

docs.title: 11. Events, logs and run metadata
docs.text:
ADR-0010: Events. One typed stream (L1) and a synchronous in-process bus.

Envelope (pipeloom.event/1): - id (uuid4 hex), run_id, invocation_id, seq (monotonic per invocation, assigned under the bus lock), ts (RFC 3339 UTC, microseconds), type, level, unit_id, model, attempt, data (typed payload), context (orchestrator ids). - Cross-invocation ordering is by (ts, invocation_id, seq).

Event types: - Run: run.started, run.compiled (plan summary), run.cancel_requested, run.completed. - Unit: unit.queued, unit.started, unit.retrying, unit.succeeded, unit.failed, unit.timed_out, unit.cancelled, unit.skipped. - Model: model.input_read, model.quality_evaluated, model.schema_changed, model.written, model.log (user ctx.log). - State: state.watermark_committed. - Other: sink.disabled, artifact.written, diagnostic (validation warnings).

Bus and sinks: - The bus fans out to sinks in the order they are configured. - Each sink has a failure_budget (default 5 consecutive errors). When exhausted, the sink is disabled and sink.disabled goes to the remaining sinks. - buffered: true wraps a sink in a bounded queue and worker thread for slow transports, with drop-oldest and a count of drops. - A redaction filter masks registered secret values before any sink sees an event. - Built-in sinks: console, jsonl (stdout or file), file (per-invocation event files under artifacts), artifacts (always on; builds the result files). - pipeloom-openlineage maps units to OpenLineage jobs: <project>.<model>, with a parent run facet for the pipeline run, the error facet, and input and output datasets from the manifest. The output-statistics facet is used if available (unverified). - RecordingSink in pipeloom.testing asserts ordered events.

Source: 05-events.d2.

Console library: rich. It provides styled tables, colors and live progress in one dependency. structlog would still need a renderer for those. JSON lines need only the stdlib.

14:02:14 finished in 2.9s | OK 3 | WARN 1 | FAIL 1 | SKIP 1 | rows written 12,573
         fct_payments  PLX101 model raised KeyError: 'amount'
                       hint: column missing in input 'payments' (ref stg_payments)
                       at src/shop/marts/payments.py:14 in build
14:02:14 artifacts: target/run_results.json, target/manifest.json, target/events.jsonl

Long engine (JVM) traces are trimmed to the first user frame and the root cause. The full trace goes to JSON events only.

Per-model metadata (run_results.results[]): - Identity: unique_id (model.<project>.<name>), unit_id, materialization, strategy, relation_name. - Status: status, attempt, retries_used. - Timing: started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, queue_wait_ms. - Rows: rows_read{input: n|null}, rows_written, rows_inserted, rows_updated, rows_deleted, rows_dropped, rows_quarantined. - Bytes and version: bytes_written, bytes_read (null unless the engine reports it), target_version. - Incremental: watermark_before, watermark_after, is_incremental, full_refresh. - Schema: schema_hash, schema_changes[]. - Quality: expectations[]{name, kind, action, passed, failed}, warnings[]. - Error: {code, category, message, hint, exception_type, trace_excerpt}. - Runtime: engine, engine_version, executor, orchestrator_ids (Databricks job, run and task run ids; Airflow dag, run, task and try), idempotency_token.

Per-run metadata (run_results.run): - run_id, parent_run_id, invocation_ids[], project, target, plan_hash, selector, args, full_refresh. - status, started_at, ended_at, duration_ms, counts{status: n}, totals{rows_written, bytes_written}. - identity{user, host, orchestrator}, pipeloom_version, plugins{name: version}, python_version, git_sha (if available), exit_code.

Metrics capture (L5): - MetricsProvider.before_write records the target version. - after_write reads commit history for versions in (before, after] and sums operation metrics. One model writes one target per run, so no global tag is needed. - Engines without history count rows instead: count on eager frames, or the writer's return value.

Artifacts. Layout: <artifacts.root>/runs/<run_id>/{manifest.json, run_results.json, events/<invocation_id>.jsonl, units/<unit_id>/attempt-<n>.json}. Local runs also copy the latest into target/. - manifest.json (pipeloom.manifest/1): metadata{pipeloom_version, plugins, config_version, plan_hash, project, target, boundary}, nodes{unique_id: resolved config, inputs, checksum}, sources, units{unit_id: [unique_ids]}, parent_map, child_map, selectors. - run_results.json (pipeloom.run_results/1): metadata, args, run, results[]. - Finalize merges unit files and picks the latest attempt per unit. Run records also go to the state store for history.

docs.title: 12. The Databricks plugin
docs.text:
pipeloom-databricks depends on pipeloom-spark and databricks-sdk. It provides the unity catalog, a databricks secret provider, the databricks-job renderer, the databricks executor (deploy and run from the CLI), and task-value publishing.

Source: 06-databricks.d2.

ADR-0011: Rendering.

Task type: each unit becomes one python_wheel_task:

{"task_key": "fct_orders", "depends_on": [{"task_key": "stg_orders"}],
 "python_wheel_task": {"package_name": "pipeloom", "entry_point": "pipeloom",
   "parameters": ["run", "--project-dir", "<synced path>", "--manifest", "<path>/manifest.json",
     "--target", "prod", "--select", "unit:fct_orders", "--expect-plan-hash", "<h>",
     "--run-id", "{{job.parameters.pipeloom_run_id}}", "--orchestrator-run-id", "{{job.run_id}}",
     "--full-refresh", "{{job.parameters.full_refresh}}"]},
 "environment_key": "pipeloom", "max_retries": 1, "min_retry_interval_millis": 60000,
 "timeout_seconds": 1800}
  • Task keys are sanitized model names: [A-Za-z0-9_-], truncated with a short hash suffix (assumed 100-character limit; verify).
  • The project is synced as workspace files by the bundle. python_paths are prepended at execution.

Compute: - Default: serverless, with one environments[] entry whose spec.dependencies pins pipeloom, pipeloom-spark and pipeloom-databricks at the running version (environment_version is an assumed field; verify). - Alternative: compute: job_cluster emits a shared job_clusters[] entry plus wheel libraries. - Per-model databricks.compute: <key> overrides. - On Databricks the engine uses the active session and never builds one.

Job lifecycle: - The default is a saved job: jobs/create, or reset when it already exists, found by tag pipeloom_job=<project>.<pipeline>.<target>, then run-now. Saved jobs give run history, repair, only-subset runs and up to 1,000 tasks. - runs/submit is used only with pipeloom databricks run --ephemeral (dev). It is limited to 100 tasks (PLD002). - Job settings: max_concurrent_runs: 1, queueing enabled, parameters pipeloom_run_id (default empty) and full_refresh (default false), tags carrying plan_hash.

Bundles: - pipeloom databricks bundle --target prod --out resources/ writes resources/pipeloom_<project>.job.yml, which is deterministic and diff-friendly. databricks bundle deploy remains the user's step. - The same render(plan) -> JobSettings dict also feeds pipeloom databricks deploy (direct SDK) for users without bundles. - A load_resources hook for Python bundle resources is on the roadmap.

Run identity and metadata: - An empty pipeloom_run_id resolves to dbx-<job.run_id>. Repairs keep the same job run id, so the pipeloom run_id is stable and the attempt number increments. - Each task writes its unit file to artifacts.root (a UC Volume path); this is the source of truth. - Each task also calls taskValues.set("pipeloom", {...}) with status, rows written, duration, target version, warnings and error code, capped well under 48 KiB, for UI visibility and {{tasks.<k>.values.pipeloom}} conditions. - A final task pipeloom__finalize (pipeloom finalize --run-id ...) depends on all leaves with run_if: ALL_DONE. It writes run_results.json and closes the run. - Model tasks keep run_if: ALL_SUCCESS, which maps skip-downstream onto Databricks "upstream failed".

Task limit: - jobs/create allows up to 1,000 tasks including finalize. - Above the limit the plan fails with PLD001, with the hint to set databricks.task_grouping: by_tag | by_folder. That fuses models into multi-model units run with --select unit:<group>, which the in-process scheduler runs as a sub-plan. Alternatively, split into separate pipelines by selector. - No automatic job chaining before 1.0.

Subset and reruns: - pipeloom databricks run --select tag:x resolves to task keys plus finalize and calls run-now with only. - pipeloom databricks repair --run-id calls the repair API with all failed tasks and their dependents.

docs.title: 13. The Airflow plugin
docs.text:
pipeloom-airflow supports Airflow ≥ 3.0 only. It imports from airflow.sdk import DAG, TaskGroup, BaseOperator, BaseSensorOperator, Asset. Triggers come from the Airflow 3 trigger base (verify the module path per minor version).

from pipeloom_airflow import PipeloomDag, ProjectConfig, RenderConfig, ExecutionConfig, ExecutionMode, LoadMode

shop_daily = PipeloomDag(
    dag_id="shop_daily", schedule="@daily", start_date=datetime(2026, 1, 1),
    project_config=ProjectConfig(project_dir="/opt/pipelines/shop", manifest_path="/opt/pipelines/shop/target/manifest.json"),
    target="prod",
    render_config=RenderConfig(load_method=LoadMode.MANIFEST, select=["tag:daily"], group_by="folder", emit_assets=True),
    execution_config=ExecutionConfig(mode=ExecutionMode.DATABRICKS, databricks_conn_id="databricks_default"),
)

PipeloomTaskGroup takes the same configs inside an existing DAG.

ADR-0012: Airflow rendering.

Load methods (parse time): - MANIFEST (recommended): reads a precompiled manifest.json. - PROJECT: compiles YAML. This is safe because no user code runs (ADR-0003), and it is cached by a hash of the inputs. - Neither imports engines or connects to anything.

Execution modes: - LOCAL: PipeloomRunOperator per unit runs pipeloom run --manifest ... --select unit:<id> --run-id <rid> in a subprocess. - VIRTUALENV: the same, using a prebuilt venv path. - KUBERNETES: wraps KubernetesPodOperator from the cncf provider extra with a user image. - DATABRICKS: described below. - DOCKER: later.

Shared behavior: - One Airflow task per unit. Airflow retries own the retry count. - Trigger rule all_success, so skip-downstream maps to upstream_failed. - A pipeloom_finalize task runs with all_done. - rid is af- plus 16 hex characters of sha256(dag_id + Airflow run_id), stable across task retries. A clear-and-rerun of failed tasks therefore continues the same pipeloom run. - With emit_assets, each model task declares Asset(uri=<target URI>) outlets.

Source: 07-airflow-modes.d2.

Databricks mode. - Options: (a) DatabricksWorkflowTaskGroup with DatabricksTaskOperator children; (b) one run-now of the bundle-deployed job, with per-model status mirroring. - Option (a) builds the job spec from Airflow operators at parse time. That duplicates the pipeloom renderer, forces job name <dag_id>.<group_id>, fixes max_concurrent_runs=1, and disables "Repair All Failed Tasks" on Airflow 3. - Choice: (b). - A deferrable launch task (PipeloomDatabricksRunOperator) finds the job by tag, or creates it from the manifest at run time with ensure_job=True. It calls run-now with job_parameters {pipeloom_run_id: rid} and pushes the Databricks run id to XCom. - If a terminal Databricks run already exists for rid and has failures (for example after a cleared launch), it calls repair with all failed tasks instead. - Each model gets a deferrable PipeloomDatabricksTaskSensor that mirrors the task state of its task_key: success, failed (error excerpt from the unit artifact), or skipped (AirflowSkipException for upstream-failed or excluded tasks). - The sensors keep the plan's dependencies, so the Airflow graph is the pipeline graph. - Consequences: one job definition whether the run is triggered by Airflow, the Databricks UI or the CLI, and repair stays in Databricks. Airflow task retries of a sensor only re-poll; reruns go through launch. Polling load is about one call per sensor per interval, with a configurable interval and an optional shared poll cache in launch's XCom.

docs.title: 14. Security and secrets
docs.text:
• Secrets never appear as literals in YAML. Fields whose names match secret patterns accept only ${secret:...} or ${env:...} (PLS104).
  • ${secret:<provider>/<path>} resolves at runtime inside the executing process through the pipeloom.secret_providers group. Providers: env (core), file (core, mode-checked), databricks (secret scopes), airflow (connections and variables).
  • The manifest, events and artifacts store only the references. Resolved values are registered with the redaction filter.
  • Discovery never imports plugins until a config names them. PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD exists for locked-down hosts.
  • Supply chain:
  • Trusted publishing (OIDC) with PEP 740 attestations.
  • Actions pinned by commit SHA, with Dependabot updates.
  • No pull_request_target workflows.
  • Integration secrets only in protected environments, never for fork PRs.
  • Private vulnerability reporting through SECURITY.md.
  • Grants are declared in YAML and applied by the catalog. pipeloom never escalates privileges.

docs.title: 15. Testing, CI, release, docs
docs.text:
Tests: - Unit tests per package. - Property tests (hypothesis) for the scheduler: random DAGs, injected failures and timeouts. Invariants: a unit starts only after all parents succeed; every unit reaches exactly one terminal state; no level barrier, checked with timed fakes. - Golden tests for the manifest and diagnostics. - CLI tests for every flag via click.testing.CliRunner (L4). - A synthetic, deterministic "shop" dataset (customers, orders, payments) generated in pipeloom.testing.data.

Engine contract suite (pipeloom.testing.contract.EngineContract). Every engine plugin subclasses it with a factory fixture, and each test is skipped unless the matching capability is declared. It covers: - read for each declared format; - logical-type round trip; - sql alias binding; - each strategy, including merge deletes, SCD2 history and replace_partitions; - the idempotent retry of each strategy with the same token; - the schema-change policy matrix; - incremental filter_since and max_value; - evaluate counts against a reference; - metrics fields that are non-null where declared; - cancel stops long work; - session cleanup restores settings (L10).

Catalog, state-store and sink contract suites follow the same pattern.

Renderer tests: - Databricks: snapshot JSON and YAML, the limits, and task-key sanitizing. - Airflow: DAG-bag parse with no network access, with a parse-time budget, and per-mode task graphs. - Live Databricks and Airflow tests run only in a manually dispatched workflow.

CI: - ruff check and format; mypy --strict; pytest with coverage. - Matrix: Python 3.11-3.14 on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS. Spark tests on Ubuntu with Java 17. - uv build plus installing the wheel into a clean venv plus pipeloom --version. - Docs build with --strict and D2 compile.

Release (ADR-0016): - SemVer per distribution, with lockstep versions for first-party distributions during 0.x and one tag vX.Y.Z. - The tag workflow checks that the tag equals the version, builds, then publishes to PyPI by trusted publishing through the protected pypi environment, then creates the GitHub release with notes from CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog). - config_version, the manifest and event schema versions, and the plugin API version are versioned separately.

Docs: - mkdocs-material with mkdocstrings (API), mkdocs-click (CLI), generated error-code and JSON Schema pages, and D2-rendered SVGs. - Versioned with mike on GitHub Pages. - ADRs in docs/adr/.

docs.title: 16. Roadmap
docs.text:
• 0.0.2: reserve the name; skeleton (section 18); CI, release, governance; this document and the ADRs.
  • 0.1: config models, loader with line marks, L0-L6, graph, selectors (name, +name, name+, tag:, path:, materialized:), plan, manifest, schema export, event bus with console and jsonl sinks. CLI: validate, compile, ls, graph, schema, plugins. A MemoryEngine for tests.
  • 0.2: scheduler, thread and process executors, pipeloom-polars and pipeloom-pandas, table/view/ephemeral, append and overwrite, sqlite and json state, run_results, the contract suite.
  • 0.3: incremental, merge, replace_partitions, schema-change policy, expectations and quarantine, retries, timeouts, cancellation.
  • 0.4: pipeloom-spark (Delta and Spark Connect), metrics from commit history, intermediates, idempotent writes, the table state store.
  • 0.5: pipeloom-databricks: renderer, bundle YAML, deploy, run, repair, finalize, task values, task grouping.
  • 0.6: pipeloom-airflow: LOCAL, VIRTUALENV and KUBERNETES modes, then DATABRICKS mode.
  • 0.7: pipeloom-openlineage, SCD2, deletes, pipeloom retry (result:fail+), state:modified.
  • 0.8-0.9: hardening, performance, docs completeness, API freeze candidates, the deprecation policy.
  • 1.0: config_version: 1, plugin API 1.0, manifest, event and run_results schemas v1 all declared stable.

docs.title: 17. ADR list and diagrams
docs.text:
Each ADR is Context, Options, Choice, Consequences, as written in the sections above.

ADR Topic Where 0001 Record architecture decisions docs/adr/ 0002 Engine abstraction: protocols plus Narwhals helpers §5 0003 Model authoring: YAML plus Python or SQL, declared inputs §4 0004 Plugin discovery via entry points; eight groups §6 0005 Packaging (see below) §17 0006 Ready-queue scheduler §8 0007 Data handoff: execution units, inlining, intermediates §8 0008 Incremental key, watermark state, strategies §9 0009 Expectations and quarantine §10 0010 Events, sinks, artifacts; rich for the console §11 0011 Databricks job rendering §12 0012 Airflow rendering and modes §13 0013 Run identity, idempotency, reruns (see below) §17 0014 Secrets by reference §14 0015 Python ≥ 3.11; click CLI; pydantic v2; hatchling; mypy strict §17 0016 Versioning, release, plugin API version §15

ADR-0005: Packaging. - Options: - One distribution with extras. Its entry points are registered even when the extra's dependencies are missing, which leads to import errors at load. It also couples dependency bounds. - Separate distributions in separate repos: high overhead. - Separate pipeloom-<plugin> distributions in one uv workspace. - Choice: the uv workspace. The core is distribution pipeloom at the repo root; plugins live in plugins/pipeloom-<name>/ with import package pipeloom_<name> (no namespace packages). - Convenience extras on pipeloom (for example pipeloom[polars]) just depend on the plugin distribution. - PyPI now: publish pipeloom 0.0.2 only. Plugin names get published with their first functional release, which avoids PEP 541 placeholder squatting. - Pending trusted publishers may be registered for the plugin names. Assumption: a pending publisher does not reserve a name; verify. - [tool.uv.workspace] is added in 0.2 with the first plugin (whether uv accepts an empty members glob is unverified).

ADR-0013: Run identity. - run_id is either caller-supplied or generated as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-<6 hex>, matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}. - Orchestrators derive it deterministically: dbx-<job_run_id> or af-<hash>. - Orchestrator retries and repairs keep the run_id and increment the attempt. - Local pipeloom retry --from <run_id> creates a new run with parent_run_id, selecting result:fail+ (failed units plus their skipped descendants). - Writes are idempotent through the token <run_id>:<model>.

ADR-0015: Python version. Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026, so the floor is 3.11.

D2 diagrams (docs/diagrams/): 1. 01-context.d2: users, YAML project, CLI and API, engines, catalogs, orchestrators, event consumers. 2. 02-packages.d2: distributions, core modules, import direction, the entry-point groups each plugin fills. 3. 03-lifecycle.d2: load → validate → resolve → validate plan → compile → execute → finalize, with the artifacts and error prefixes of each stage. 4. 04-state-machines.d2: unit and run state machines, including retry, timeout, skip and cancel transitions. 5. 05-events.d2: event bus fan-out to sinks, redaction, failure budget, buffered sinks, the artifact writer. 6. 06-databricks.d2: plan → job settings or bundle YAML; tasks, finalize, run-id propagation, artifacts on the volume, task values. 7. 07-airflow-modes.d2: PipeloomDag in LOCAL/KUBERNETES mode (one task per unit) versus DATABRICKS mode (launch, mirror sensors, repair path).

docs.title: Verification plan (for the skeleton commit)
docs.text:
• uv sync && uv run pytest -q && uv run mypy --strict src && uv run ruff check

docs.title: Risks
docs.text:
• The orchestrator thread executor's timeouts are cooperative. Code that ignores cancellation keeps running until the process ends.
  • In Airflow DATABRICKS mode the sensors poll per model. Large DAGs need a longer poll interval or the shared poll cache.
  • Unverified facts are marked inline: serverless environment_version, the task-key length limit, whether pending publishers reserve names, pydantic's draft-2020-12 output, whether uv accepts an empty workspace, and the OpenLineage output-statistics facet. Verify each before implementing it.
  • Narwhals stable-API drift: pinning to stable.v2 limits it.
  • Lockstep versioning means plugin-only fixes still bump every distribution during 0.x.

docs.title: Resolved defaults (2026-10-29)
docs.text:
1. Airflow 3 only (ADR-0012).
  2. Only pipeloom is published now. Plugin names are published with their first functional release (ADR-0005).
  3. Docs and JSON Schema URLs live at https://emanuel-luis.github.io/pipeloom/. The repo has been public since 2026-11-02.
  4. DCO sign-off. The author and CODEOWNERS are Emanuel Luis. Security reports go through GitHub private vulnerability reporting or email.

docs.title: Context
docs.text: pipeloom is designed before it is built, and plugin authors and contributors need to see why each choice was made, not only what it is. Decisions made in chat or in a pull request thread get lost. The architecture document (architecture.md) holds the full design, but a single long document is hard to amend one decision at a time.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Decisions only in the architecture document. One place to read. Changing one decision means editing a long page, and the reason a choice was made drifts away from its date.
  • A wiki or issue tracker. Easy to edit, but it lives outside the repository, so it is not versioned with the code and not reviewed in pull requests.
  • One ADR file per decision in docs/adr/. Versioned and reviewed with the code. Short files with a fixed shape. Needs a little discipline to keep the index current.

Numbers are never reused. A decision that changes gets a new ADR that supersedes the old one, and the old ADR's status changes to Superseded. README.md is the index.

docs.text:
• Every decision has a stable link that issues, pull requests and docs can cite.
  • A new ADR goes through the same review as code.

docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0002: Engine abstraction: protocols plus Narwhals helpers
docs.text: Architecture: Section 5, Core protocols

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Moving from one engine to several couples code in the return type of a model, reads, schema, temporary views, writes, merge, metrics and catalog SQL. The core needs one contract that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins can all meet, without forcing Spark users into a lowest common denominator.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• (a) A hand-written protocol per plugin. Full control over IO, writes and metrics. More code per engine.
  • (b) Narwhals as the core abstraction. Small and dependency-free, but it has no write, SQL or catalog API, and only supports lazy PySpark.
  • (c) Ibis. Broad engine coverage, but heavy. Its write support is unverified, and it pushes users into an expression API.
  • (d) A hybrid. Hand-written protocols for the contract, Narwhals only for portable helpers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Option (d).

  • The core contract is the hand-written protocols (Engine, EngineSession, Reader, Materializer, Catalog, MetricsProvider and others). Plugins own IO, writes, merge, catalogs, metrics and cancellation.
  • The core depends on Narwhals only for pipeloom.engine.portable. That module gives default count, filter_since, max_value, schema and evaluate that pandas, polars and PySpark plugins may reuse, through narwhals.stable.v2.
  • Model bodies receive native frames by default. frame_api: narwhals on a model passes Narwhals frames, so portable models work on any engine with capabilities.portable.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No lowest-common-denominator API for Spark users.
  • Engines can override the portable defaults for speed.
  • Narwhals stays a replaceable implementation detail. Pinning to stable.v2 limits API drift.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0003: Model authoring: YAML plus Python or SQL, declared inputs
docs.text: Architecture: Section 4, Configuration

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Declared dependencies (lesson L2) and YAML validation (L14) are core principles. Users still need a real transformation language.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• YAML only. Easy to validate, but too weak for transformations.
  • YAML plus Python. Full power, but SQL users must wrap queries in code.
  • YAML plus SQL. Familiar for SQL users, but no escape for logic SQL cannot express.
  • YAML plus both. Covers both audiences. Needs a rule for how inputs reach the body.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
YAML plus both. YAML declares every model. The body is either a Python callable or a SQL body. The inputs map binds local aliases to ref or source.

  • A Python callable is called as build(ctx, **inputs). Each alias becomes a keyword argument holding a relation.
  • SQL refers to aliases as table names. The engine registers them as named relations for that query only.
  • At compile time pipeloom imports nothing from the project. Validation layer L6 parses the callable's file with ast to check that the function exists and that its parameters equal ctx plus the input aliases.
  • Opt-in SQL table-reference checking through the sqlglot extra warns on mismatch.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Graphs are cheap to build, so Airflow can parse DAG files safely.
  • No Jinja templating.
  • Reads of undeclared tables through ctx.engine.native are a documented escape hatch outside lineage.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0004: Plugin discovery via entry points; eight groups
docs.text: Architecture: Section 6, Plugin system and plugin API version

docs.title: Context
docs.text: pipeloom needs engines, catalogs, state stores, sinks, secret providers, executors, renderers and naming strategies to be supplied by separately installed distributions, without the core importing them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Entry points (stdlib importlib.metadata, the pytest model). No new dependency.
  • pluggy. Built for 1:N hook fan-out.
  • A dbt-style namespace import. Couples plugin layout to import paths.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Entry points. pipeloom picks one implementation per role by kind, which is 1-of-N selection, not hook fan-out, so pluggy adds a dependency without a matching need.

  • Eight groups: pipeloom.engines, pipeloom.catalogs, pipeloom.state_stores, pipeloom.sinks, pipeloom.secret_providers, pipeloom.executors, pipeloom.renderers, pipeloom.naming.
  • Each entry point resolves to a PluginSpec(name, kind, api_version, factory, config_model, compatible_engines).
  • Discovery reads metadata only. A plugin is imported only when a config names its kind. pipeloom plugins list imports nothing.
  • PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 restricts loading to --plugin module:spec.
  • A duplicate kind within a group is error PLU002.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• No extra dependency, and listing plugins is safe on locked-down hosts.
  • Plugins are versioned against the plugin API version (ADR-0016).
  • No hook fan-out. If a later feature needs it, this ADR must be revisited.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0005: Packaging
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0005 text

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The core and the engine, orchestrator and lineage integrations have different dependencies and release needs. Users should install only what they run.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• One distribution with extras. Its entry points are registered even when the extra's dependencies are missing, which leads to import errors at load. It also couples dependency bounds.
  • Separate distributions in separate repositories. High overhead.
  • Separate pipeloom-<plugin> distributions in one uv workspace.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The uv workspace.

  • The core is distribution pipeloom at the repo root. Plugins live in plugins/pipeloom-<name>/ with import package pipeloom_<name> (no namespace packages).
  • Convenience extras on pipeloom (for example pipeloom[polars]) just depend on the plugin distribution.
  • PyPI now: publish pipeloom 0.0.2 only. Plugin names are published with their first functional release, which avoids PEP 541 placeholder squatting.
  • Pending trusted publishers may be registered for the plugin names. Assumption: a pending publisher does not reserve a name (unverified).
  • [tool.uv.workspace] is added in 0.2 with the first plugin. Whether uv accepts an empty members glob is unverified.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One repository and one lockfile, with separate dependency bounds per plugin.
  • Plugin names stay unclaimed on PyPI until their first functional release, so someone else could register one in the meantime.
  • Lockstep versions apply during 0.x (ADR-0016).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0006: Ready-queue scheduler
docs.text: Architecture: Section 8, Execution and scheduler

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Running a graph level by level makes every unit in a level wait for the slowest one (lesson L6). Scheduling must be deterministic so runs are reproducible and testable.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Level barriers. Simple, but idle workers wait at each level.
  • A ready queue with no level barrier. Starts a unit as soon as its parents are done.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
A ready-queue scheduler with no level barrier.

  • When a unit reaches a terminal state, each child's count of pending parents goes down by one. A child whose count reaches zero is enqueued.
  • Ready units are ordered by descending count of downstream units, then by name, which is deterministic.
  • workers caps concurrency. pool tags (a later milestone) cap per-resource concurrency.
  • Policies: retries with exponential backoff and jitter (transient errors only unless retry_on: any), per-unit timeouts, cooperative cancellation with cancel_grace, skip-downstream by default with --fail-fast as an option, and a StateStore.lock concurrency guard per project and target.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Property tests (hypothesis) check the invariants: a unit starts only after all parents succeed, and every unit reaches exactly one terminal state.
  • Thread-executor timeouts are cooperative: code that ignores cancellation keeps running until the process ends. The process executor kills the child.
  • With boundary: task the orchestrator owns retries.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0007: Data handoff: execution units, inlining, intermediates
docs.text: Architecture: Section 8, ADR-0007

docs.title: Context
docs.text: With boundary: task, each unit runs in its own process or orchestrator task, so no in-memory or temporary-view handoff is possible (lesson L7).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Persisted intermediates everywhere. Simple, but costs IO.
  • Inlining everywhere. No extra IO, but recomputes shared work.
  • A hybrid, decided at compile time.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
The hybrid.

  • ephemeral models are inlined. Their bodies run inside each consuming unit. Under boundary: process the result is memoized per run, so it is computed once.
  • intermediate models are persisted to <artifacts.root>/runs/<run_id>/intermediate/<model> (or a scratch schema the catalog provides). Finalize deletes them after intermediate_ttl.
  • view creates a catalog view where the engine supports it, never a session view.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The same plan runs in one process or many.
  • PLP406 warns when an ephemeral model fans out to more than ephemeral_fanout_warn (default 3) units and suggests intermediate.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0008: Incremental key, watermark state, strategies
docs.text: Architecture: Section 9, Incremental processing, write strategies, schema change

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Incremental logic must be declared, not inferred (lesson L12), and must survive crashes and orchestrator retries. Every write option must be applied by each strategy or rejected (L9).

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Watermark kept in the target (max(column) of the target). No extra store, but needs the target to exist and read access to it.
  • Watermark in a StateStore with compare-and-swap. Works for targets that cannot be queried cheaply, at the cost of a store.
  • Both, selected per model with watermark_source: state | target.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
A declared key plus a lookback, with watermarks in a StateStore. watermark_source: target reads max(column) of the target instead.

  • Per unit: determine is_incremental, read the watermark w, filter the input with filter_since(input, column, w - lookback), write, then cas_watermark(expected=w, new=max_value(filtered input)). A CAS failure is PLM203.
  • State stores: sqlite (core, local), json (core, atomic rename), table (spark plugin). boundary: task requires table or json on a shared path.
  • Strategies: append, overwrite, replace_partitions, merge, scd2. Each returns a WriteResult.
  • Idempotency: each write receives token = "<run_id>:<model>". Engines without idempotent writes declare idempotent_writes=False.
  • on_schema_change: fail (default), ignore, append_new_columns, sync_all_columns.
  • Maintenance (optimize, vacuum, clustering) runs only from maintenance: blocks, never by default.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The watermark is committed after the write. A crash between the two reprocesses at most the lookback window plus the batch. That is safe for merge, overwrite and replace_partitions, and for append only when the engine has idempotent writes (otherwise PLC505 forbids retries).
  • A schema change under the default policy fails the unit (PLM202). Every detected change emits model.schema_changed.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0009: Expectations and quarantine
docs.text: Architecture: Section 10, Data quality

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Data quality is a first-class feature (lesson L13). Rules need a clear action when a row or a dataset violates them, and failing rows should not vanish silently.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Fail-only checks. Simple, but one bad row stops the run.
  • DLT-style actions (warn, drop, fail) plus quarantine. Lets users choose per rule, and keeps dropped rows for inspection.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
DLT-style actions plus quarantine, evaluated after the transformation and before the write.

  • Row-level checks: not_null, accepted_values, range, regex, expr. Actions: warn, drop, fail.
  • Aggregate checks: unique, row_count, freshness. Actions: warn, fail. drop is PLP403.
  • EngineSession.evaluate computes every row-level predicate in one aggregate pass and returns per-expectation passed and failed counts. Unlike DLT, counts are kept on fail too.
  • drop filters rows that fail any drop predicate. If max_drop_ratio is exceeded, the unit fails with PLQ301.
  • With quality.quarantine: true, dropped rows go to <target>__quarantine with _pipeloom_run_id, _pipeloom_failed and _pipeloom_ts.
  • Lazy engines may cache the relation before the counting pass. The engine decides, and the decision is recorded in the metadata.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Results appear in run_results.json and in model.quality_evaluated events.
  • Expressions in expr checks use the engine's dialect and are not portable.
  • A quarantine table is extra storage that users must manage.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0010: Events, sinks, artifacts; rich for the console
docs.text: Architecture: Section 11, Events, logs and run metadata

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Logs, metrics, artifacts and lineage should not each have their own plumbing (lesson L1). Runs must also leave structured metadata that can be queried later.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Separate logging, metrics and lineage paths. Each is simple alone, but they drift apart.
  • One typed event stream with subscribers.
  • Console library: rich gives styled tables, colors and live progress in one dependency. structlog would still need a renderer for those. JSON lines need only the stdlib.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
One typed stream (pipeloom.event/1) and a synchronous in-process bus.

  • The envelope carries id, run_id, invocation_id, seq, ts, type, level, unit_id, model, attempt, data and context. Cross-invocation ordering is by (ts, invocation_id, seq).
  • The bus fans out to sinks in configured order. Each sink has a failure_budget (default 5 consecutive errors). When exhausted the sink is disabled and sink.disabled goes to the remaining sinks.
  • buffered: true wraps a sink in a bounded queue and worker thread, with drop-oldest and a count of drops.
  • A redaction filter masks registered secret values before any sink sees an event.
  • Built-in sinks: console, jsonl, file, artifacts (always on). pipeloom-openlineage maps units to OpenLineage jobs.
  • The console uses rich. JSON lines use the stdlib.
  • Artifacts: manifest.json (pipeloom.manifest/1) and run_results.json (pipeloom.run_results/1), with per-model and per-run metadata.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Any consumer (console, files, lineage) is a sink, and tests can assert ordered events with RecordingSink.
  • A slow sink on the synchronous bus slows the run unless it is buffered.
  • JVM traces are trimmed on the console. The full trace goes to JSON events only.
  • The OpenLineage output-statistics facet is used if available (unverified).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0011: Databricks job rendering
docs.text: Architecture: Section 12, The Databricks plugin

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A plan must run as one Databricks job, with run history, repair and the platform's own scheduling, and the same plan must also run locally.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• One task per unit as python_wheel_task, in a saved job. Gives run history, repair, only-subset runs and up to 1,000 tasks.
  • runs/submit (ephemeral). No saved job, but limited to 100 tasks and no repair history. Kept for --ephemeral dev runs.
  • Fewer, fused tasks. Needed only above the task limit (databricks.task_grouping).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Each unit becomes one python_wheel_task running pipeloom run --manifest ... --select unit:<id> --expect-plan-hash <h> --run-id ....

  • Task keys are sanitized model names, truncated with a short hash suffix (assumed 100-character limit, unverified).
  • Compute: serverless by default, with one environments[] entry pinning the pipeloom distributions to the running version (environment_version is an assumed field, unverified). compute: job_cluster is the alternative.
  • The default is a saved job found by tag pipeloom_job=<project>.<pipeline>.<target>: jobs/create, or reset when it exists, then run-now. Settings: max_concurrent_runs: 1, queueing, parameters pipeloom_run_id and full_refresh.
  • pipeloom databricks bundle writes a deterministic resources/pipeloom_<project>.job.yml. pipeloom databricks deploy uses the SDK directly.
  • An empty pipeloom_run_id resolves to dbx-<job.run_id>. Each task writes its unit file to artifacts.root and publishes taskValues (capped well under 48 KiB). A final pipeloom__finalize task (run_if: ALL_DONE) writes run_results.json.
  • Above 1,000 tasks the plan fails with PLD001 and a hint to use task grouping or split by selector. No automatic job chaining before 1.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One job definition, whether it is triggered from the CLI, the Databricks UI or Airflow (ADR-0012).
  • Repair keeps the job run id, so the pipeloom run_id is stable and the attempt number increments.
  • pipeloom databricks run --select resolves to task keys plus finalize and uses only.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0012: Airflow rendering and modes
docs.text: Architecture: Section 13, The Airflow plugin

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Teams that orchestrate with Airflow need the pipeline graph as DAG tasks, with Airflow retries, assets and the same run identity as other orchestrators. Airflow DAG files are parsed often, so parsing must be safe and cheap.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
For the DATABRICKS mode:

  • (a) DatabricksWorkflowTaskGroup with DatabricksTaskOperator children. Builds the job spec from Airflow operators at parse time. That duplicates the pipeloom renderer, forces job name <dag_id>.<group_id>, fixes max_concurrent_runs=1, and disables "Repair All Failed Tasks" on Airflow 3.
  • (b) One run-now of the bundle-deployed job, with per-model status mirroring.

For the plugin overall: support Airflow 2 and 3, or Airflow 3 only.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Airflow 3 only (airflow.sdk, version >= 3.0). Dropping Airflow 2 support was accepted on 2026-10-29.

  • Load methods: MANIFEST (recommended) reads a precompiled manifest.json. PROJECT compiles YAML, which is safe because no user code runs (ADR-0003). Neither imports engines or connects to anything.
  • Modes: LOCAL, VIRTUALENV, KUBERNETES (wraps KubernetesPodOperator), DATABRICKS. DOCKER is later.
  • Shared behavior: one Airflow task per unit with Airflow owning retries, trigger rule all_success, a pipeloom_finalize task with all_done, and rid = af- plus 16 hex of sha256(dag_id + Airflow run_id), stable across task retries. With emit_assets, each model task declares Asset outlets.
  • DATABRICKS mode uses (b). A deferrable launch task finds or creates the job and calls run-now with pipeloom_run_id = rid, or repair if a failed run exists for rid. Each model gets a deferrable sensor that mirrors the state of its task_key.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• One job definition however the run is triggered, and repair stays in Databricks.
  • Airflow task retries of a sensor only re-poll. Reruns go through launch.
  • Polling load is about one call per sensor per interval, with a configurable interval and an optional shared poll cache.
  • The shared artifact store for LOCAL and KUBERNETES modes is still open, with fsspec as the leading option (decide in 0.6).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0013: Run identity, idempotency, reruns
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0013 text

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A run can span several processes and orchestrator tasks, and tasks can be retried or repaired. Metadata, events and writes from all of them must join into one run, and a retry must not duplicate data.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• A fresh run_id per attempt. Simple, but splits one logical run into many.
  • A stable run_id with an attempt counter, derived deterministically by orchestrators.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• run_id is either caller-supplied or generated as YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ-<6 hex>, matching [A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,64}.
  • Orchestrators derive it deterministically: dbx-<job_run_id> or af-<hash>.
  • Orchestrator retries and repairs keep the run_id and increment the attempt.
  • Local pipeloom retry --from <run_id> creates a new run with parent_run_id, selecting result:fail+ (failed units plus their skipped descendants).
  • Writes are idempotent through the token <run_id>:<model>.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• A cleared-and-rerun Airflow task continues the same pipeloom run.
  • Engines without idempotent writes declare idempotent_writes=False, and validation forbids retries on non-idempotent append (PLC505).
  • Run records go to the state store for history.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0014: Secrets by reference
docs.text: Architecture: Section 14, Security and secrets

docs.title: Context
docs.text: YAML files, manifests, events and artifacts are committed, logged and shared. Secret values must never end up in them.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Literal secrets in YAML. Convenient, and unsafe.
  • Environment variables only. Safe, but no integration with platform secret stores.
  • References resolved at runtime through providers.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Secrets by reference.

  • Fields whose names match secret patterns accept only ${secret:...} or ${env:...}. A literal is PLS104.
  • ${secret:<provider>/<path>} resolves at runtime inside the executing process through the pipeloom.secret_providers group. Providers: env and file (core, mode-checked), databricks (secret scopes), airflow (connections and variables).
  • The manifest, events and artifacts store only the references. Resolved values are registered with the redaction filter (ADR-0010).
  • Discovery never imports plugins until a config names them. PIPELOOM_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD exists for locked-down hosts.
  • Grants are declared in YAML and applied by the catalog. pipeloom never escalates privileges.
  • Supply chain: trusted publishing (OIDC) with PEP 740 attestations, actions pinned by commit SHA, no pull_request_target workflows, integration secrets only in protected environments, and private vulnerability reporting through SECURITY.md.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The compile-time manifest is safe to share. Secrets exist only in the running process.
  • ${secret:...} is not resolved at compile time, so a bad reference shows up at run time (or in --preflight).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0015: Python 3.11 or newer; click CLI; pydantic v2; hatchling; mypy strict
docs.text: Architecture: Section 17, ADR-0015 text, and section 18

docs.title: Context
docs.text: A new public project started in late 2026 must pick a Python floor and a base toolchain. Python 3.10 reaches end of life in October 2026.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Python floor: 3.10 (reaches end of life in October 2026) or 3.11.
  • CLI: click (the 0.0.2 skeleton depends on click>=8.1).
  • Config models: pydantic v2, which also exports the JSON Schema (section 4).
  • Build backend: hatchling.
  • Types: mypy in strict mode.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: Python 3.11 or newer, click for the CLI, pydantic v2 for config models, hatchling as the build backend, and mypy --strict in CI. CI runs Python 3.11 to 3.14 on Ubuntu, Windows and macOS.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Code may use 3.11 features, and users on 3.10 cannot install pipeloom.
  • The package has one runtime dependency (click) at 0.0.2.
  • pyproject.toml and CI follow this ADR.
  • While the repo was private, CI ran one Windows and one macOS job on 3.12 only, to save macOS minutes. The full matrix returned when the repo went public on 2026-11-02.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: ADR-0016: Versioning, release, plugin API version
docs.text: Architecture: Section 15 (Release) and section 6 (Plugin API version)

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Several distributions ship from one repository, and several contracts evolve at different speeds: the package, the plugin protocol, the config format and the manifest, event and run_results schemas.

docs.title: Options
docs.text:
• Lockstep versions for first-party distributions during 0.x, with one tag. Simple releases. Plugin-only fixes still bump every distribution.
  • Independent versions per distribution. Precise, but more release work and a larger compatibility matrix while the API is moving.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
• SemVer per distribution, with lockstep versions for first-party distributions during 0.x and one tag vX.Y.Z.
  • The tag workflow checks that the tag equals the version, builds, then publishes to PyPI by trusted publishing through the protected pypi environment, then creates the GitHub release with notes from CHANGELOG.md (Keep a Changelog).
  • config_version, the manifest and event schema versions, and the plugin API version are versioned separately.
  • pipeloom.plugins.API_VERSION = (MAJOR, MINOR), independent of the package version. MINOR covers additive changes. MAJOR covers breaking protocol changes. The core accepts plugins with the same MAJOR and MINOR not above its own, otherwise it raises PLU001.
  • Before 1.0 the plugin API is 0.x and any minor may break. Plugin API 1.0 ships with pipeloom 1.0.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Plugin authors can target a plugin API version instead of a package version.
  • Lockstep versioning means plugin-only fixes bump every distribution during 0.x.
  • At 1.0, config_version: 1, the plugin API 1.0, and the manifest, event and run_results schemas v1 are declared stable.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted
